chapter: Players and bands of old New Orleans
title: The Durand-Humphrey band era and the Newman family
summary: Laurent recalls the Alamo and Music Box, a pianist and his young trumpeter son who later played in New York with Erskine Hawkins.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask one more question about the old time bands.

Now I was playing at the time when Duran and Humphrey band was together. And then that time. I was playing all over that time. They were playing at the Alamo. And at the Music Box. Then, how you call that boy used to be in your room? His daddy taught him to play music. He played that trumpet so well. Dwight Newman.

Well, Dwight Newman. Good piano. Great piano. Pianist. And he had the job at the Music Box. He had a little son. Was in my wife's room. My wife teaches public school. Joseph. Joseph. You talking about the trumpet player. You know, you ain't play high side on the trumpet. Just like you played on the clarinet. He could play it on trumpet like that. He was a good little player. And he was no bigger than that. Oh, he was good. He was good. He was good. He's gone, I bet. Yeah, oh, he's in New York. He's in New York. Great inside up in New York. He's a good guy. He was a good guy. He was a good guy. He was a good guy. He was a good guy. He was a good guy. He's gone, I bet.
Yeah, oh, he's in New York. He's in New York.
Where'd you sign up in New York somewhere?

But, he's been in New York for a very long time. You know, as a young fellow. He's done very well. He was with, um, whose name was that? The same thing Mary's husband was with. His last name starts with an H. Not Heinz. Let's see.
Hawkins, Erskine Hawkins. Hawkins, Erskine Hawkins.
That's the band here. That's the band here. Erskine Hawkins.
